en.title: Number of Stable Contiguous Periods with At Most k Income Values
en.description:
A non-empty contiguous period of the income array is stable if it contains at most k distinct income values. Count all stable periods modulo 1000000007; periods with different start or end positions are counted separately.

The standard I/O, examples and editorial were written independently by this site; ranges explicitly marked as this site's are not the source's original constraints.
en.input: The first line contains n k; the second line contains the incomes. 1≤n≤100000, 1≤k≤n, −10^9≤income≤10^9.
en.output: Output a single integer, the answer.
en.explanation: The answers are 3, 10 and 6. A contiguous range of equal incomes may also span multiple dates.
hints: Maintain each value's frequency in a sliding window and shrink the left end whenever there are more than k distinct values; each right end contributes the window length.
